name: PHerc0343P fragment, 3 segments (no model at letter level here)
summary: Native 8.64 µm / 116 keV surface volumes; reference = 2.215 µm new_canon map. Reader v2/V3 are scored only on their two held-out segments; d9v4C is shown but excluded (leak). Caveat: the main reference is the canonical 2 µm model's prediction, not ground truth; node R checks it against letters traced on an infrared photograph (an independent, camera-based reference). Scope: PHerc0343P is a fragment that detached from PHerc. 343 during mechanical unwrapping; it has its own scans (8.64 µm 20250510090703, 2.215 µm 20250512023932). None of the 3 segments overlaps Nieuwlaar's PHerc. 343 region (scan 20250509220833, windings w047/w048, z 9500-11000).

nodes.question: Does the model see known ink on this labelled segment?
nodes.answer: PARTLY: significant agreement but not letter-level for every held-out checkpoint (WEAK).
evidence: Brackets: 95% CIs from a 2 mm tile bootstrap that keeps the registration fixed. They give precision, not significance; significance is the shift-null p-value.
Held-out checkpoints: 0 PASS, 11 WEAK, 2 FAIL (best: dense_native @511003658, r_bp 0.28, stroke recall 0.16 vs chance 0.06; recall − chance +0.10, 95% CI [+0.00, +0.20]).
Excluded from the verdict (segment in their training data): d9v4C @233748, d9v4C @172054.
nodes.next_step: Ask whether the scan explains the loss (node B), then whether it is the scan or the scroll (node C).

nodes.question: Do independent references agree with each other and on the model verdicts?
nodes.answer: YES: all 8 agreement tests pass, so the verdict does not hinge on one reference.
evidence: References: **new_canon 2.2 µm map** (canonical team model prediction on a 4× finer scan of segment 20250511003658); **IR-traced letters** (letters traced by the Vesuvius Challenge team on an infrared photograph of the fragment, placed on the 8.64 µm scan by D. Russo (DomRusso2/ir-truth-9um); independent of any CT model, but only 8 traced strokes in the overlap).
team 2.2 µm map vs IR letters (AUC): ir-truth-9um scorer, null = 2000 random placements of the letter mask (results/irtruth/ir_scores.json).
team 2.2 µm map vs IR letters (inkcheck): inkcheck PASS against the IR letters (results/irtruth/inkcheck/team2.2um_vs_IR.json): the IR reference can return PASS when letters are present.

Ranking: dense_native 0.770/0.741, dense9um (Klavis) 0.753/0.695, seed42 0.632/0.601, seed43 0.651/0.674, soup 0.662/0.618. Metric fixed before the IR runs. With band-pass r instead of AUC the rank correlation is 0.7 (not significant with 5 models). The IR set is small (its README: too small to rank models that score close together), so read the ranking as supporting evidence only. Reader V2/V3 are not ranked here: both were trained on 20250511003658.
Same prediction scored against each reference; 'same decision' = both PASS or both not PASS.

nodes.question: Do this scan's quality proxies fall outside what a ~9 µm model tolerates?
nodes.answer: NO: every proxy is inside the tolerated range, so scan blur/noise alone does not explain the loss.
evidence: Tolerance curve: Paris 4 dose-response (dense_native, docs/RESOLUTION_STUDY.md; proxies from study/psd_compare.py and study/layer_snr.py).
HF spectral ratio (10–25 / 2–10 cyc/mm): sharpness proxy; Paris 4 still PASSes with added blur FWHM ≈ 23 µm (ratio 0.024).
adjacent-layer high-pass correlation: noise proxy (it rises with blur, so it is read only against the noise curve); Paris 4 still PASSes with noise σ = 0.5× volume SD (0.32).
Stroke size is not the issue either: the median 343P reference stroke (≈ 0.19 mm²) is comparable to the Paris 4 reference strokes (results/study/stroke_geometry.json; Paris 4 values withheld).
nodes.next_step: Test scan vs scroll directly (node C): same segment, second scan.

nodes.question: Same segment, two scans: is it the scan or the scroll?
nodes.answer: SCROLL/INK (scored segments only): no checkpoint reaches letter level on either scan, so on these segments the gap is not voxel size or scan protocol.
evidence: 5 checkpoints scored on both scans; median Δ r_bp +0.05, median Δ stroke recall -0.06.
nodes.next_step: Change the model or the labels, not the scan: on these segments a finer or cleaner scan is not the bottleneck. This covers only the segments scored; other regions of the same scroll can behave differently, so test them with node A.

recommendation: Change the model or the labels, not the scan: on these segments a finer or cleaner scan is not the bottleneck. This covers only the segments scored; other regions of the same scroll can behave differently, so test them with node A.
headline: On these 3 segments of the detached fragment PHerc0343P, no held-out model reaches letter level (WEAK; seed42 FAIL), including Reader v2/V3 on their own held-out segments; the scan is inside the tolerated blur/noise range and a 4× finer scan of the same segment does not fix it, so the gap here is segment/ink-specific, not resolution. This does not extend to the rolled scroll PHerc. 343: the same public 9 µm models read letters there (E. Nieuwlaar, First Letters prize, Oct 2026; different object, scan and region).
